title: Structural Analysis and Statics
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Structural Analysis and Statics.
notes: Equilibrium and reactions

Isolate the structure, identify support constraints and all external actions, then apply force and moment equilibrium. Symmetry may simplify reactions, but only after the load and support geometry are verified.
Beams and diagrams
Distributed loads reduce to resultants for reactions; shear is the derivative of moment, so a smooth interior moment extremum occurs where shear is zero. Preserve sign conventions consistently.
Trusses and resultants
At ideal pin joints, resolve member forces along member axes. Zero-force rules require the stated joint loading and connectivity; they are not visual guesses.
Stability and deformation
Euler buckling is an ideal elastic model sensitive to effective length. Deflection formulas require their stated load, support, small-deformation, and prismatic-member assumptions.

title: Strength and Mechanics of Materials
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Strength and Mechanics of Materials.
notes: Stress, strain, and stiffness
Average normal stress is axial force divided by area; elastic strain is stress divided by modulus and elongation is strain times original length. Keep force and area units compatible.
Section response
The centroidal second moment for a rectangle is bd cubed over 12 about the axis parallel to b. Elastic bending stress equals moment divided by section modulus at the extreme fiber.
Combined and local effects

A hole reduces net area and can raise local elastic stress through a stated concentration factor. Offset loads add moments; fatigue models combine mean and alternating stress only under their declared assumptions.
Material interpretation
Concrete cylinder strength is failure load divided by specimen area. Ductility, stiffness, fatigue resistance, and strength describe different behaviors and should not be substituted for one another.

title: Applied Mathematics for Civil Engineering
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Applied Mathematics for Civil Engineering.
notes: Model setup
Translate geometry, rates, percentages, and unit scales into one consistent system before calculating. Check dimensions and estimate the expected magnitude.
Optimization and calculus
Differentiate a continuous response to locate candidate extrema, then check the allowed interval and endpoints. Integrate rates over the stated interval to obtain accumulated quantities.
Ratios and scaling
Map scale, grade, productivity, density, and utilization are ratios with different denominators. Write the numerator and denominator labels before inserting values.
Data interpretation
Use tables and trends as evidence within their measured range. A departure from linearity, uncertainty interval, or limiting constraint must be interpreted rather than merely copied.

title: Surveying, Leveling, and Layout
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Surveying, Leveling, and Layout.
notes: Scale and direction
Convert map length using the representative fraction and compatible units. Distinguish azimuth from an interior or deflection angle before applying a turn.
Leveling

Height of instrument equals known elevation plus backsight; the next elevation equals height of instrument minus foresight. Arithmetic closure checks observations but does not identify every field blunder.
Traverse components
Resolve each line into latitude and departure with consistent signs; algebraic sums show closure error or net displacement, depending on whether the traverse is intended to close.
Field control
Protect benchmarks, record observations in sequence, repeat critical checks, and connect layout to a documented datum rather than an assumed local reference.

title: Transportation and Highway Engineering
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Transportation and Highway Engineering.
notes: Traffic stream variables
Flow, speed, and density satisfy q=kv under a consistent macroscopic model. Average values and observation intervals must refer to the same traffic stream.
Signals and capacity
An idealized approach capacity can be estimated from saturation flow times effective-green ratio; compare demand with that capacity before inferring oversaturation.
Horizontal alignment
For a simple circular curve, tangent length is R tan(delta/2) with delta in the angle convention expected by the calculation.
Grades and profiles
Percent grade is rise over horizontal run times 100. A change from positive to negative grade forms a crest profile; the reverse forms a sag profile.

title: Construction Quantities and Productivity
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Construction Quantities and Productivity.
notes: Quantity takeoff
Compute geometric quantities in consistent dimensions, then apply material rates. Separate direct quantity changes from overhead, profit, waste, and contractual adjustments unless supplied.
Productivity
Productivity is output divided by the relevant labor, equipment, or elapsed-time input. Compare crews on the same basis and include utilization when converting theoretical to effective capacity.
Method control
A workable method statement connects sequence, resources, interfaces, hazards, quality checks, and acceptance responsibilities; a schedule alone does not control execution risk.
Records and change
Document measured quantities, assumptions, approvals, and affected work. A unit-price quantity change uses the supported incremental quantity before other contract effects are considered.

title: Fluid Mechanics, Pipe Flow, and Open Channels
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Fluid Mechanics, Pipe Flow, and Open Channels.
notes: Hydrostatics
Pressure head and pressure use p=gamma h; resultant hydrostatic force on a plane area uses pressure at its centroid. Buoyancy equals displaced-fluid weight.
Continuity and energy
For incompressible steady flow, discharge equals area times mean velocity. Total head combines elevation, pressure, and velocity heads, while losses reduce available head along real systems.
Pumps
Hydraulic power is rho g Q H; required shaft power divides hydraulic power by efficiency. Cavitation assessment requires suction-side pressure and vapor-pressure context.
Open channels
Hydraulic radius is area divided by wetted perimeter. Froude number and specific energy distinguish subcritical, critical, and supercritical states under the stated section assumptions.

title: Soil Properties, Effective Stress, and Seepage
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Soil Properties, Effective Stress, and Seepage.
notes: Phase relationships
Water content is water mass over dry-soil mass; void ratio is void volume over solid volume. Unit weight, density, porosity, and void ratio are related but not interchangeable.
Classification and compaction

Grain-size measures and Atterberg limits support standardized classification. A compaction curve identifies maximum dry unit weight and its corresponding optimum water content for the specified effort.
Effective stress and strength
Effective stress is total stress minus pore pressure. Mohr–Coulomb strength combines cohesion and effective-normal-stress friction under the stated drained or undrained model.
Seepage
Darcy discharge is permeability times hydraulic gradient times area. Exit gradients near or above critical values indicate piping or heave concern, not a guaranteed failure time.

title: Foundations, Settlement, and Stability
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Foundations, Settlement, and Stability.
notes: Bearing and contact pressure
Average footing pressure is service load divided by plan area. Allowable-capacity comparisons must keep service and ultimate bases distinct and use the stated safety factor.
Settlement
Consolidation settlement follows compressibility, layer thickness, stress history, drainage, and time. A void-ratio relation is valid only with the defined initial condition and strain convention.
Slopes and retaining systems

Factor of safety compares available resistance with driving actions on the assumed mechanism. Water pressure and seepage alter both loading and effective stress, so drainage can be structurally significant.
Failure interpretation

General shear commonly shows a defined failure surface and ground heave; punching is more localized. Rapid loading of saturated clay is often assessed with an undrained model when drainage cannot occur.

title: Civil Engineering Data and Laboratory Interpretation
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Civil Engineering Data and Laboratory Interpretation.
notes: Tables and trends
Identify controlled and measured variables, units, and the comparison basis before selecting a trend. Do not infer causation or extrapolate beyond the supplied data without support.
Laboratory response
Initial linearity can establish a reference slope; departure, scatter, and outliers require checking calibration, specimen behavior, and repeatability before assigning a mechanism.
Derived parameters
Compute ratios such as permeability comparisons, strength slopes, or intercepts from consistent test conditions. A larger input does not imply a larger response when another governing factor changes.
Reporting
Retain significant figures appropriate to the data, state assumptions, and distinguish observed results from model-based interpretation.

title: Construction Safety, Materials, and Quality
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Construction Safety, Materials, and Quality.
notes: Quality control and assurance
Field tests verify that placed work meets the project basis; they supplement process control rather than substitute for documented requirements and representative sampling.
Concrete and durability

Curing preserves moisture and temperature conditions needed for hydration. Marine chloride exposure calls for a coherent durability strategy addressing permeability, cover, cracking, materials, and detailing without inventing a universal limit.
Execution safety

Method review should identify sequence, temporary conditions, interfaces, hazards, controls, hold points, and responsibilities. Compliance values come from the governing project and jurisdiction, not generic study notes.
Evidence and decisions
Investigate nonconforming or unusual results before assigning cause. Use calibrated tests, traceable records, and acceptance criteria appropriate to the work.

title: Hydrology, Water Supply, and Drainage
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Hydrology, Water Supply, and Drainage.
notes: Demand and storage
Convert per-capita demand and population to daily volume, then apply explicitly stated losses and balancing duration. Keep demand, production, and storage periods distinct.
Runoff estimation
The rational method combines runoff coefficient, rainfall intensity, and drainage area with a unit-conversion constant; it assumes the supplied intensity and catchment representation are appropriate.
Hydrographs
Runoff volume over an interval is area under discharge above the selected baseflow. With equal intervals, compare average excess ordinates rather than one peak alone.
Drainage reasoning
Drainage systems manage collection, conveyance, storage, and safe discharge. Capacity conclusions require the relevant storm, boundary conditions, losses, and downstream controls.

title: Structural Testing and Nondestructive Evaluation
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Structural Testing and Nondestructive Evaluation.
notes: Test planning
Define the property, expected response, load range, instrumentation, and acceptance basis before testing. Calibration and repeatability are prerequisites to interpreting small differences.
Response interpretation
Compare measured response with the initial trend and an appropriate model; nonlinearity can indicate several mechanisms and should not be assigned a cause without corroboration.
Nondestructive methods
Liquid penetrant reveals surface-breaking discontinuities in suitable nonporous materials; other methods are selected for subsurface, volumetric, or material-specific targets.
Limits of evidence
An indication is not automatically a defect, and a nondetection is not proof of absence. Method sensitivity, access, geometry, preparation, and operator procedure bound conclusions.

title: Engineering Economics and Project Scheduling
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Engineering Economics and Project Scheduling.
notes: Economic equivalence
Compare cash flows at a common time using the stated interest rate and timing convention. NPV subtracts the initial investment from discounted benefits and costs.
Cost models

Straight-line depreciation spreads depreciable basis over service life; equivalent annual cost converts alternatives to a common annual basis. These models do not replace technical feasibility checks.
Network scheduling
A finish-to-start network duration follows the longest controlling path. Recalculate path floats after duration or logic changes rather than assuming the original critical path remains controlling.
Decision records
State analysis period, price basis, included costs, assumptions, and uncertainty. Nominal undiscounted totals and present worth answer different questions.

title: Reinforced Concrete, Steel, and Connections
summary: Concept-focused Civil Engineering review covering governing relationships, assumptions, units, interpretation, and common reasoning errors for Reinforced Concrete, Steel, and Connections.
notes: Reinforced-concrete behavior

Concrete is strong in compression but weak in tension, so longitudinal reinforcement crosses tensile regions and develops force through bond. Reinforcement ratio uses steel area divided by the stated concrete reference area.
Members and limit states
Beam, column, and connection behavior depends on load path and failure mode. Keep service demand, factored demand, nominal capacity, and any explicitly supplied reduction separate.
Steel members and connections

Gross yielding, net-section behavior, shear, tension, weld throat, eccentricity, and resultant actions are distinct checks. Use only the resistance expression and factors supplied or authoritatively specified.
Ductility and seismic response
Repeated reversals favor stable inelastic deformation and energy dissipation. Ductility does not mean unlimited deformation or remove the need for strength and detailing checks.

title: Cost Behavior, CVP, Sales Mix, and Sensitivity
summary: Technical management-accounting foundation for fixed and variable cost behavior, contribution analysis, break-even reasoning, sales mix, and decision sensitivity.

notes.heading: Cost behavior
notes.body: Separate fixed, variable, and mixed cost behavior using the facts supplied. A contribution margin is sales less variable cost; fixed costs are then considered in operating-income and break-even analysis.

notes.heading: CVP and mix reasoning
notes.body: Use unit contribution, contribution margin ratio, margin of safety, and weighted contribution consistently. When products have different margins, preserve the stated sales mix before drawing a break-even conclusion.

notes.heading: Sensitivity
notes.body: Test how a stated change in volume, price, variable cost, or fixed cost changes the decision. A sensitivity result is conditional on the supplied assumptions; it does not establish an outcome outside them.

title: Relevant Costs and Short-Term Decisions
summary: Decision-focused coverage of avoidable, opportunity, and sunk costs for make-or-buy, special-order, and constrained-resource decisions.

notes.heading: Relevant information
notes.body: Include only future revenues and costs that differ between alternatives. Unavoidable past or allocated amounts do not become relevant merely because they appear in a full-cost report.

notes.heading: Decision comparisons
notes.body: For make-or-buy and special-order decisions, compare incremental effects and identify capacity consequences. An opportunity cost is the contribution sacrificed when a scarce resource is committed elsewhere; a sunk cost is not recoverable and is excluded.

notes.heading: Constraints
notes.body: When a resource is limiting, compare contribution per unit of the constrained resource and check demand and feasibility before selecting the mix.

title: Operating and Cash Budgeting
summary: Technical coverage for operating budgets, flexible planning, cash forecasts, and financing requirements.

notes.heading: Operating budgets
notes.body: Build sales, production, and cost expectations from the stated volume and price assumptions. Keep operating-income calculations separate from cash timing.

notes.heading: Cash planning
notes.body: A cash budget begins with opening cash, adds expected collections, subtracts expected payments, and compares the result with the required minimum. Financing is the amount needed to close an actual shortfall, not the full payment total.

notes.heading: Interpretation
notes.body: A budget is a decision model under stated assumptions. Investigate deviations by separating volume, price, timing, and controllability rather than treating every variance as an error.

title: Standard Costs and Variance Analysis
summary: Concept-fit support for standard quantities and prices, price and usage variances, and careful favorable/unfavorable interpretation.

notes.heading: Variance inputs
notes.body: Identify the standard and actual quantity, price, rate, or hours before calculating a variance. State whether the comparison uses the quantity purchased, quantity used, or flexible-budget activity level.

notes.heading: Direction and interpretation
notes.body: A cost above its standard is unfavorable when the same basis is used. A variance is a signal for investigation; it does not by itself establish responsibility or cause.

notes.heading: Decision use
notes.body: Combine variance amounts with operational context and controllability before recommending corrective action.

title: Responsibility, Control, Performance, and Quality Costs
summary: Managerial performance support for controllability, responsibility centers, performance measures, and cost-of-quality analysis.

notes.heading: Responsibility and control
notes.body: Evaluate a manager using revenues and costs the manager can reasonably influence. Distinguish a controllable margin from a full segment result when the question identifies controllability.

notes.heading: Performance measures
notes.body: Use operational and financial measures together, identify the decision context, and avoid treating one metric as proof of overall performance.

notes.heading: Cost of quality
notes.body: Classify prevention, appraisal, internal-failure, and external-failure costs before comparing them. A cost-of-quality report describes process and quality performance; it is not activity-based costing unless cost pools and drivers are supplied.

title: Capital Budgeting and Present Value
summary: Decision support for payback, present value, net present value, and the distinction between cash-flow measures.

notes.heading: Investment measures
notes.body: Payback compares the initial investment with periodic cash inflows and ignores time value when the question says so. Present value discounts future cash flows using the supplied factor or rate.

notes.heading: NPV reasoning
notes.body: Net present value is the present value of future cash inflows and outflows, including the initial investment. Keep a requested present-value subtotal distinct from NPV.

notes.heading: Judgment
notes.body: Use only the cash flows and assumptions supplied. A positive or negative result supports the stated decision rule but does not establish facts beyond the model.

title: Activity-Based Costing and Cost Drivers
summary: Technical foundation for activity pools, cost-driver rates, product assignments, and comparison with broad-volume allocation.

notes.heading: Pools and drivers
notes.body: Group overhead by activity, identify the driver that explains resource use, calculate a pool rate, and assign cost from the product’s actual driver usage. Do not substitute a broad production volume when the activity driver is stated.

notes.heading: Allocation reasoning
notes.body: Compute each activity rate separately before summing assignments. The assigned amount is a product-cost estimate for the supplied activities, not proof that the product caused every organizational cost.

notes.heading: Interpretation
notes.body: Compare ABC and traditional allocations only when both bases and the relevant volumes are supplied. Use the resulting information to investigate product or customer profitability rather than treating allocation as a cash cost.

title: Engineering mathematics
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for engineering mathematics, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Model selection and units
notes.body: Translate the stated geometry or physical relation into variables first, keep units consistent, and test whether the requested result is a value, rate, vector magnitude, or dimensionless quantity.

notes.heading: Calculus and optimization
notes.body: Derivatives give instantaneous rates and locate candidate extrema; definite integrals accumulate a rate over an interval. Verify endpoints and physical constraints before accepting an optimum.

notes.heading: Linear algebra and system behavior
notes.body: A determinant tests singularity for a square system, while eigenvectors identify directions whose orientation is preserved by a linear transformation. Pole location and residual patterns diagnose dynamic stability and model inadequacy.

notes.heading: Data and uncertainty
notes.body: Use averages only for the intended population, interpret confidence-interval width as uncertainty rather than error, and treat convergence or residual patterns as evidence about a method rather than proof of the underlying model.

title: Engineering sciences
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for engineering sciences, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Dimensional reasoning
notes.body: Mechanical power has dimensions of energy per time, so force times velocity and torque times angular speed are consistent forms. Dimensional agreement is necessary but does not by itself validate a model.

notes.heading: Electrical response
notes.body: For series AC resistance and inductive reactance, combine perpendicular impedance components by magnitude; distinguish impedance from resistance and keep phase behavior separate from scalar addition.

notes.heading: Measurement response
notes.body: Calibration points support linearity only over the observed range. Examine slope, scatter, uncertainty, and residual pattern before extrapolating or claiming exact behavior.

notes.heading: Engineering evidence
notes.body: When an input property has wide measured spread, propagate or bound that uncertainty and obtain representative data when the decision is sensitive; do not hide variability behind a single nominal value.

title: Statics and dynamics
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for statics and dynamics, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Free-body discipline
notes.body: Isolate the body, show every external force and couple, choose axes, and only then write equilibrium or motion equations. A missing action cannot be repaired by later algebra.

notes.heading: Work, impulse, and momentum
notes.body: Net work changes kinetic energy; external impulse changes momentum. Conservation statements apply only after defining a system and checking the corresponding external transfer.

notes.heading: Rotation and mechanisms
notes.body: Torque is force times perpendicular moment arm. Angular acceleration follows change in angular velocity over time, while natural frequency reflects the ratio of stiffness to inertia.

notes.heading: Two-dimensional motion
notes.body: Resolve projectile velocity into orthogonal components, use the same elapsed time for each direction, and apply level-ground range relations only when their stated assumptions hold.

title: Mechanics of materials
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for mechanics of materials, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Stress and strain
notes.body: Average axial stress is load divided by area. Elastic modulus is the initial stress–strain slope, Poisson ratio connects lateral and axial strain, and thermal strain is alpha times temperature change when expansion is free.

notes.heading: Combined loading
notes.body: At a critical point, superpose compatible axial and bending normal stresses with their signs; do not compare either component alone with a limit when both act simultaneously.

notes.heading: Bending and deflection
notes.body: Section modulus converts bending moment to extreme-fiber stress. Energy methods can obtain selected deflections without integrating the entire elastic curve when their assumptions are satisfied.

notes.heading: Columns and joints
notes.body: Euler load varies inversely with effective-length squared for the ideal elastic column. Weld throat area, load path, and stress type must be identified before calculating joint demand.

title: Fluid mechanics
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for fluid mechanics, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Flow conservation
notes.body: Volumetric flow is mean velocity times area for a filled section. A momentum balance uses mass flow and the vector change in velocity to obtain the force associated with a turning jet.

notes.heading: Pressure, buoyancy, and losses
notes.body: Hydrostatic gauge pressure is rho g h; buoyancy equals displaced-fluid weight. Darcy loss scales with friction factor, length-to-diameter ratio, and velocity head.

notes.heading: Internal-flow interpretation
notes.body: Reynolds number identifies the applicable regime; fully developed circular-pipe laminar flow has a parabolic profile whose centerline speed is twice the mean. Property trends must be read from supplied data without inferring an unrelated regime.

notes.heading: Pumps and similarity
notes.body: Read a pump curve as head versus flow for a stated configuration. For unchanged diameter under ideal affinity laws, flow scales with speed, head with speed squared, and power with speed cubed; cavitation symptoms prompt an available-suction-head check.

title: Thermal science
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for thermal science, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Energy accounting
notes.body: For a closed system, heat added minus work done by the system gives the internal-energy change under the stated sign convention. For steady devices, use the control-volume energy balance and retain only terms the problem permits neglecting.

notes.heading: Properties and ideal gases
notes.body: An ideal gas of fixed mass obeys pressure proportional to absolute temperature at fixed volume. A throttling device is modeled as approximately constant enthalpy only under steady, adiabatic, negligible-work and negligible kinetic/potential-change assumptions.

notes.heading: Entropy and compression
notes.body: Friction and other irreversibilities generate entropy. Intercooling between compression stages reduces required work by lowering the specific volume entering a later stage.

notes.heading: Cycles and combustion
notes.body: Thermal efficiency is net work divided by heat input. Ideal Otto and Diesel models differ in their heat-addition process, and combustion accounting begins with a balanced fuel–oxidizer reaction before energy calculations.

title: Heat transfer
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for heat transfer, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Resistance networks
notes.body: For one-dimensional steady heat flow, series thermal resistances add and heat rate equals the driving temperature difference divided by total resistance.

notes.heading: Convection and extended surfaces
notes.body: Convection rate is hA times the surface-to-fluid temperature difference. Fins help when the extra effective area more than offsets their temperature decline and contact limitations.

notes.heading: Radiation
notes.body: Ideal blackbody emissive power is proportional to absolute temperature to the fourth power; Celsius values cannot be substituted into that relation.

notes.heading: Heat exchangers
notes.body: A cold stream can approach but not exceed the hot inlet temperature in an ordinary passive exchanger. Use Q=UA times the log-mean temperature difference when U, area, flow arrangement, and terminal temperatures support that model.

title: Power systems
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for power systems, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Shaft power
notes.body: Rotating mechanical power is torque times angular speed; convert revolutions per minute to radians per second before multiplying.

notes.heading: Turbines and cycles
notes.body: For an adiabatic turbine with negligible kinetic and potential changes, specific work follows the enthalpy drop. For a complete cycle, net work divided by heat input gives thermal efficiency.

notes.heading: Boiler auxiliaries
notes.body: An economizer recovers exhaust-gas energy to preheat feedwater, reducing the fuel energy needed for the same steam duty without treating the recovered heat as free work.

notes.heading: Performance boundaries
notes.body: State idealizations explicitly, distinguish shaft output from thermal input, and retain device efficiency when converting between fluid power and required shaft power.

title: Refrigeration and HVAC
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for refrigeration and hvac, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Refrigeration performance
notes.body: Refrigerator COP is heat removed from the cold space divided by work input; it is not a thermal efficiency and may exceed one.

notes.heading: Moist-air interpretation
notes.body: At fixed dry-bulb temperature, increasing humidity ratio generally raises relative humidity. Sensible heat ratio equals sensible load divided by total sensible-plus-latent load.

notes.heading: Compressor capacity
notes.body: Volumetric efficiency relates actual intake volume to ideal displacement; divide actual delivered intake volume by volumetric efficiency to infer required ideal displacement.

notes.heading: Humidity control
notes.body: When temperature is acceptable but moisture is excessive, prioritize latent cooling or dehumidification rather than adding sensible cooling that does not address the moisture load.

title: Machine design
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for machine design, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Design against failure
notes.body: Select criteria for the actual load history: endurance behavior for repeated stress, instability for slender columns, contact or wear for interfaces, and yielding or fracture for peak stress.

notes.heading: Shafts, springs, and clutches
notes.body: Use the stated torsion relation with torque and diameter in compatible units. Spring energy is one-half kx squared; ideal multi-surface clutch capacity scales with surface count, friction coefficient, axial force, and effective radius.

notes.heading: Fatigue models
notes.body: Mean and alternating stress must be combined using the specified fatigue relation. A Goodman calculation is a model-based safety factor, not proof of infinite life.

notes.heading: Brakes, welds, and materials
notes.body: Hot brake fade indicates temperature-dependent loss of friction. Weld demand uses effective throat area, while material choice weighs environment, strength, manufacturability, and life-cycle degradation rather than one property alone.

title: Machine elements
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for machine elements, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Gear kinematics and force
notes.body: For an external gear pair, speed varies inversely with tooth count. Tangential pitch-line force equals transmitted torque divided by pitch radius, with torque and radius in consistent units.

notes.heading: Belts and chains
notes.body: Belt traction depends on friction and wrap together with usable tension. Chain speed follows sprocket teeth times pitch times revolutions per unit time, converted to the requested linear unit.

notes.heading: Bearings and lubrication
notes.body: Bearing selection considers equivalent load and accumulated duty, while overheating also requires checking lubricant viscosity, supply, contamination, alignment, and generated heat.

notes.heading: Power-transmission checks
notes.body: Trace torque, speed, force, and power through the component interfaces; distinguish kinematic ratios from capacity limits and efficiency losses.

title: Manufacturing processes
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for manufacturing processes, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Cutting rate and power
notes.body: Ideal cutting power is cutting force times cutting speed. Turning speed is circumference times revolutions per unit time, and linear feed is feed per revolution times rotational speed.

notes.heading: CNC setup
notes.body: A workpiece datum establishes the coordinate reference that connects the programmed tool path to the actual part; verify fixturing and offsets before execution.

notes.heading: Tolerance accumulation
notes.body: For worst-case end-to-end dimensions, add nominal lengths and add absolute tolerances for the extreme bounds unless a statistical assembly model is explicitly specified.

notes.heading: Process choice
notes.body: Match machine, tool, material, geometry, finish, tolerance, and production volume; a computed speed or feed remains subject to machine and tooling limits.

title: Industrial engineering
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for industrial engineering, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Flow and bottlenecks
notes.body: System throughput cannot sustainably exceed its slowest required station. Identify the longest cycle time, then compare it with takt or required cycle time derived from available production time and demand.

notes.heading: Inventory decisions
notes.body: EOQ balances annual ordering and holding costs under its simplifying assumptions; use the supplied demand, order cost, and unit holding cost without treating the result as universally optimal.

notes.heading: Pull production
notes.body: A kanban authorizes replenishment or movement based on downstream consumption, limiting work in process rather than serving as a forecast-only production order.

notes.heading: Capacity and improvement
notes.body: Measure acceptable output over actual operating time, locate the binding constraint, and improve or rebalance it before optimizing non-bottleneck stations.

title: Maintenance and quality
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for maintenance and quality, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Reliability models
notes.body: For a constant failure rate, exponential reliability is R(t)=exp(-lambda t), with MTBF=1/lambda. Use the model only when its assumptions are stated and interpret sparse failure intervals cautiously.

notes.heading: Condition and preventive maintenance
notes.body: Trending vibration can justify investigation before a threshold is crossed. Planned inspection and lubrication are preventive actions; condition evidence can refine timing without guaranteeing failure prediction.

notes.heading: Process quality
notes.body: Greater spread reduces capability even when the mean stays centered. A point beyond three-sigma control limits signals special-cause investigation, not automatic proof of a specific cause.

notes.heading: Safe intervention
notes.body: Before guard removal, isolate hazardous energy, control stored energy, and verify the safe state under the applicable procedure; production urgency does not replace energy control.

title: Engineering economics
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for engineering economics, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Cash-flow comparison
notes.body: Compare alternatives on a common time basis and include relevant acquisition, operating, energy, maintenance, and residual cash flows rather than choosing by first cost alone.

notes.heading: Present worth
notes.body: Discount future cash flows to the selected comparison date. For a uniform end-of-period series, multiply the recurring amount by the supplied present-worth factor when its rate and number of periods match.

notes.heading: Economic assumptions
notes.body: State the analysis period, interest rate, timing convention, and included costs. A numerical result is conditional on those assumptions rather than an intrinsic property of the machine.

notes.heading: Decision interpretation
notes.body: Prefer the economically favorable feasible alternative after technical, safety, and service requirements are met; a lower modeled cost does not excuse a design that fails those requirements.

title: Philippine Civil Code: Obligations, Contracts, Sales, and Remedies
summary: Concept-fit legal foundation for contract formation, obligations, sales, validity, remedies, and partnership relationships under the Philippine Civil Code.

notes.heading: Application boundary
notes.body: Analyze the supplied consent, authority, performance, breach, and remedy facts before drawing a legal conclusion. Do not treat a general label or a business practice as proof of a statutory result.

notes.heading: Contracts and obligations
notes.body: Use the parties' assent, definite subject, consideration, contractual terms, and timing to evaluate formation and performance. Separate a contractual obligation from a remedy that may follow a proven breach.

notes.heading: Sales and remedies
notes.body: Use the supplied delivery, conformity, notice, and defect facts to identify the next legally supported response. A remedy depends on the contract and applicable law; avoid unsupported absolute outcomes.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes are a concise study aid based on Republic Act No. 386. Consult the primary text and applicable jurisprudence for the complete rule and exceptions.

title: Philippine Corporate Authority and Governance
summary: Technical study foundation for corporate powers, board authority, share transactions, formalities, and governance decisions.

notes.heading: Authority and governance
notes.body: Distinguish the corporation's separate legal authority from the internal approval and documentation required by its governing documents and applicable law. Verify authority and ratification rather than assuming a management signature is sufficient.

notes.heading: Corporate transactions
notes.body: Analyze the stated board action, shareholder or officer role, transaction purpose, and conflict facts. Do not infer a current statutory threshold or approval rule unless the source and facts supply it.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes summarize selected applications of Republic Act No. 11232 and are not a substitute for the statute, implementing rules, or official guidance.

title: Negotiable Instruments and Commercial Security
summary: Concept-fit support for negotiable-instrument status, presentment, notice, defenses, and priority analysis.

notes.heading: Instrument analysis
notes.body: Start with the instrument's form, transfer, value, good faith, notice, and presentment facts. Separate holder status from the ultimate enforceability or priority conclusion.

notes.heading: Evidence and defenses
notes.body: A favorable holder-status fact does not erase every defense or procedural requirement. Identify the supplied issue and apply the relevant statutory condition without adding unstated facts.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes summarize selected applications of Act No. 2031. Consult the primary Negotiable Instruments Law for complete requirements and exceptions.

title: Philippine Accountancy Practice, Records, and Confidentiality
summary: Professional and statutory foundation for accountancy practice, working papers, records, confidentiality, disclosure, and professional responsibility.

notes.heading: Professional scope
notes.body: Apply the Accountancy Act and professional standards to the supplied role, document, and duty facts. Do not treat every business record as a privileged document or every request as an automatic disclosure exception.

notes.heading: Records and confidentiality
notes.body: Distinguish ownership and retention of working papers, client authorization, lawful compulsory production, and other professional duties. The correct response should preserve evidence and state the applicable limitation accurately.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes are based on Republic Act No. 9298 and the Philippine professional ethics adoption material. Consult the primary law and current professional requirements for complete treatment.

title: Professional Ethics, Conflicts, and Disclosure
summary: Application-focused support for integrity, objectivity, conflicts of interest, authorized disclosure, and independent decision-making.

notes.heading: Conflict analysis
notes.body: Identify the threat to integrity or objectivity, disclose the relevant relationship, and evaluate safeguards or independent review. A conflict signal requires analysis; it does not by itself prove misconduct.

notes.heading: Disclosure decisions
notes.body: Separate authorized disclosure, disclosure required by law or professional duty, and inappropriate disclosure. State the facts needed for a conclusion rather than inventing an exception.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes are based on the Philippine Code of Ethics adoption material and Republic Act No. 9298. They are a study aid, not a replacement for the current professional code.

title: Agency: Authority, Ratification, and Principal-Agent Effects
summary: Concept-fit Philippine agency-law foundation for evaluating representation, express and implied authority, ratification, and the effect of known authority limits on the principal.

notes.heading: Agency and authority
notes.body: Analyze whether a person acts in representation with the principal's consent or authority. Distinguish express authority, implied authority from conduct, and a third party's knowledge of an express limit before concluding whether the principal is bound.

notes.heading: Ratification
notes.body: When an unauthorized act is presented, assess the principal's subsequent conduct and acceptance of the benefit under the governing agency provisions. Acceptance may support ratification, but the conclusion remains tied to the supplied facts and applicable law.

title: Philippine Taxable Income, Bases, Deductions, and Exclusions
summary: Concept-fit support for tracing receipts and adjustments to the supplied taxable base while separating substantiation, deductions, exclusions, and period assumptions.

notes.heading: Build the tax base
notes.body: Start with the taxpayer and period, identify included receipts, then apply only the deductions or exclusions supported by the facts and governing rule. A supplied exercise rate is not evidence of a current statutory rate.

notes.heading: Substantiation and reconciliation
notes.body: Reconcile accounting records to the tax schedule and verify documentary support before accepting an adjustment. Keep recognition, classification, and computation as separate decisions.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: Use the current National Internal Revenue Code and applicable BIR issuances for live-law rates, thresholds, effective dates, and exceptions.

title: Philippine Business Taxes, VAT, and Withholding Analysis
summary: Concept-fit support for separating VAT output/input analysis, withholding roles, business-tax classification, and supplied transaction data.

notes.heading: Classify before computing
notes.body: Identify the transaction, taxpayer role, tax base, and whether an amount is output tax, input credit, withholding, or a separate business tax before calculating.

notes.heading: Withholding and VAT
notes.body: A withholding agent's remittance obligation and the payee's tax position are related but not interchangeable. Follow the applicable current Code section and BIR issuance.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: Current rates and digital-service rules require the current Tax Code amendments and BIR implementation guidance.

title: Philippine Transfer Taxes and Exemption Analysis
summary: Concept-fit support for estate and donor transfer-tax bases, exclusions, documentary evidence, and fact-specific exemption analysis.

notes.heading: Construct the transfer base
notes.body: Separate the gross transfer or estate value from deductions and legally supported exclusions. Do not assume that a label such as gift or inheritance resolves the tax treatment without checking the transaction facts.

notes.heading: Evidence matters
notes.body: Use the stated ownership, date, relationship, valuation, and documentary facts; unsupported exemptions should be investigated rather than applied automatically.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: Transfer-tax rates, thresholds, and exemptions are time-sensitive and must be checked against the current Code and BIR issuances.

summary: Concept-fit support for registration, filing, records, assessments, taxpayer responses, substantiation, and administrative remedies.

notes.heading: Procedural sequence

notes.heading: Records and substantiation
notes.body: A return, invoice, ledger, and supporting document answer different evidentiary questions. Preserve the record and reconcile inconsistencies before recommending a filing or protest response.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: Use the National Internal Revenue Code, current BIR issuances, and official filing instructions for live procedural requirements.

notes.heading: Current-law control

notes.heading: Professional judgment
notes.body: When records conflict or the law is unsettled, identify the missing authority, escalate appropriately, and avoid presenting an unsupported absolute answer to a client.

notes.heading: Source boundary

title: LET English Reading and Evidence Foundation
summary: Source-backed LET reading practice for main ideas, inference, evidence, purpose, tone, context clues, and text structure.

notes.heading: Evidence before inference
notes.body: Separate what a passage states from what it supports by implication. A defensible inference uses multiple relevant details and does not add outside knowledge.

notes.heading: Central idea and support
notes.body: A central idea accounts for the passage as a whole; supporting details explain, illustrate, qualify, or provide evidence for it.

notes.heading: Purpose, tone, and structure
notes.body: Purpose is the writer's communicative goal, tone is the attitude conveyed by language, and structure describes how ideas relate or develop.

notes.heading: Context and critical reading
notes.body: Use contrast, examples, definitions, and surrounding relationships to interpret words. Evaluate claims by asking whether the evidence supports the strength of the conclusion.

notes.heading: Sentence structure
notes.body: Distinguish independent and dependent clauses, then use coordination or subordination to express the intended relationship. Repair fragments, run-ons, and comma splices without changing the meaning.

notes.heading: Agreement and verb form
notes.body: Locate the grammatical subject rather than the nearest noun. Select verb forms and tense sequences that match number, time, aspect, and the relationship among actions.

notes.heading: Modifiers and reference
notes.body: Place modifiers beside the words they logically describe and supply a clear subject for introductory phrases. Check pronoun antecedent, number, and case so the intended referent is recoverable.

notes.heading: Parallelism and usage
notes.body: Keep coordinated items grammatically equivalent, compare like forms, and choose prepositions according to the stated relationship. Evaluate parts of speech by the word’s function in its sentence, not by its spelling alone.
